raw_response:
I will not spread my 6 mu too thin. With only 2 people in the house, I do better when most land follows the old cabbage-maize-spinach path that I already know, and I keep the side crops smaller. I have high schooling and 50 years in the field, so I look at it as water, fertilizer, labor, and selling time together. Cabbage takes heavy feeding and steady water, so I will put more fertilizer there and not let it get hungry. Maize is safer and cheaper, so I will keep the rate moderate but not low, because I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose ears. Spinach is short-season but responds fast to nitrogen and water, so I will feed it enough to push leaf growth. Chili brings cash but needs more spraying and more careful watering, so I will only keep 1 mu. Kidney bean fixes some nitrogen itself, so I will not push nitrogen hard there, but I will still give phosphorus and potassium for pod setting. I will stay close to what worked last year, then adjust a little upward on potash for cabbage and chili because the land gets used hard in this rotation and I do not want quality to fall.
